html:
SMTO-CMP-0008 — SMTO couldn't confirm the requested change actually happened

GUID: 538d43d4-5c9e-42eb-98c6-bc94aae61892
Slug: completion-missing-mutation-evidence
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI model said it made the change you asked for, but the only proof was its own statement or a command that showed no output. SMTO needs to see the change itself. Work already done is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the thing the task was meant to change yourself, for example open the file, page or setting and see whether it's updated. A command can finish without showing what it changed, so SMTO couldn't tell whether it worked.
  2. If the change is there, select Resume, or ask SMTO in the "Continue this conversation" box under the task to check and confirm it, then select Continue. SMTO then reads the current state as proof, without making the change a second time.
  3. If the change is missing, describe exactly what's missing in that box and select Continue. Clear instructions let SMTO do only the missing part instead of guessing.
  4. Don't select Restart task while you're unsure whether the change happened. Restart begins a fresh attempt and doesn't undo earlier actions, so the change could be made twice.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed and its reply describes the change you can see yourself.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with what you found when you checked. Check whether the earlier action already happened before anything is repeated. Don't restart the task while that is unclear.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Action completion cited no current-run result, or only self-assertions or exit-status-only Shell reads with empty stdout and stderr, so the cited evidence does not establish the requested state change (reason missing_mutation_evidence).

What this means

  • Action completion cites no current result or only self-assertions/empty read-command output that cannot establish the requested action outcome. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Action completion cites no current result or only self-assertions/empty read-command output that cannot establish the requested action outcome.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the mutation receipt and intended post-state separately from a neutral command exit or empty read.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the cited receipts in _verify_receipts and completion_evidence_candidates (src/agent_runtime/native/completion.py): action work needs a successful write or effect receipt from this request, or an observation of the intended post-state. Observe the post-state with a read that returns output and cite it alongside the original mutation receipt; do not re-run the mutation.
  • Inspect and verify the intended post-state; cite the authoritative mutation receipt.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Existing authoritative action/post-state evidence supports the exact completion claim.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
